extraction.name: MATH
extraction.description: A dataset of 12,500 challenging high school competition mathematics problems for measuring machine learning models' mathematical problem-solving ability. Each problem includes a full step-by-step solution, exact-match final answer, difficulty rating from 1 to 5, and spans seven subjects.
extraction.creator: Dan Hendrycks; Collin Burns; Saurav Kadavath; Akul Arora; Steven Basart; Eric Tang; Dawn Song; Jacob Steinhardt
extraction.publisher: 35th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2021) Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The MATH dataset was assembled from existing high school mathematics competition problems, many collected from the AoPS contests community, and organized with step-by-step solutions, subject labels, difficulty levels, and consistent LaTeX/Asymptote formatting. The auxiliary AMPS corpus was built by combining problems pulled from Khan Academy with millions of problems generated from hand-designed Mathematica scripts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source data included competition mathematics problems with full step-by-step solutions and final boxed answers, formatted in LaTeX and sometimes Asymptote, plus Khan Academy exercises and Mathematica-generated mathematics problems and solutions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Problems were categorized by subject and difficulty using AoPS conventions; each problem includes a step-by-step solution and final boxed answer.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: One subject label and one difficulty label per problem; each problem also has one step-by-step solution and one final boxed answer.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is challenging and current models perform poorly; generated step-by-step solutions can be misleading or logically wrong, model confidence is overconfident and unreliable, and scaling alone is unlikely to solve the benchmark. The paper also notes a non-recommended implication that strong performance could enable cheating on homework.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that solving the dataset would have broad practical and intellectual significance because mathematics has wide applicability, but also warns that sufficiently strong performance could have negative implications such as cheating on homework.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: MATH is intended as a benchmark to measure mathematical problem-solving ability of machine learning models, with training and test splits, and its step-by-step solutions can be used to train models to generate derivations and explanations. AMPS is intended as an auxiliary pretraining corpus for mathematics before fine-tuning on MATH.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: During AMPS pretraining, the authors upsampled Khan Academy data by a factor of 5 and downsampled Mathematica data by a factor of 2 to balance dataset size differences.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was consistently formatted in LaTeX and Asymptote, and final boxed answers were normalized with consistent formatting rules so answers could be uniquely matched for exact evaluation. Equivalent encodings, spacing, units, and factor orderings were treated as the same.
